newsitem.title: USA: Harmon says wins New Jersey transit deal.
newsitem.headline: Harmon says wins New Jersey transit deal.

text.p: Harmon Industries Inc said Thursday it won a contract worth more than $17 million from Raytheon Co unit Raytheon Infrastructure Services for control systems for a New Jersey light rail line.
The Hudson-Bergen Light Rail Transit System will link Hoboken and Bayonne, New Jersey, in an 11-mile, double track system, Harmon said in a statement.

Raytheon Infrastructure is the lead member of the 21st Century Rail Corp consortium building the line, Harmon said. Raytheon Infrastructure previously won a $1.26 billion contract from the New Jersey Transit Authority to design, build, operate and maintain the first phase of the project.

Harmon, a supplier of rail signal and control equipment for freight and transit systems, said it will design and build the project's microprocessor-based train control systems with automatic train identification and a central control computer.
Harmon president and chief executive officer Bjorn Olsson said in the statement it is the largest single contract ever awarded to Harmon Industries.
